future_directions.title: Limited generalisability

future_directions.title: Disagreement on attacks and ukraine
future_directions.question: Under which conditions does attacks and ukraine hold, and why do the studies describe it differently?
future_directions.rationale: The studies reporting on it (Kumar et al., 2024; Khoirunnisa et al., 2024) were judged mixed in Phase 3.
future_directions.next_step: Measure the outcome in the same way across the settings the studies cover, and test which differences (sample, setting, measure) explain the disagreement

future_directions.title: Transparent reporting of effects and samples
future_directions.question: How large are the effects behind the findings on Cyber Warfare, and how precisely are they estimated?
future_directions.rationale: The abstracts of Kumar et al. (2024), Lindsay (2025), Wang et al. (2024), Khan (2025) and Žilinčík et al. (2023) give no effect sizes and sample sizes.
future_directions.next_step: Report the size of each improvement over the baselines with its variation across runs, and state the datasets' sizes

future_directions.title: Empirical tests of proposed frameworks
future_directions.question: Do the frameworks and arguments that rest on no new data stand up to testing?
future_directions.rationale: Huang (2024), Ma et al. (2024), Unknown (2023), Cremer et al. (2024), Mohamed et al. (2023), Sfetcu (2024), Rosli (2025), Khoirunnisa et al. (2024) and Mohammed (2025) collected no new data.
future_directions.next_step: Derive testable predictions from each framework and check them against independently collected data

future_directions.title: Reproducible evaluation
future_directions.question: Would the conclusions on Cyber Warfare change under the evaluation standards of engineering, computing and the natural sciences?
future_directions.rationale: Phase 2 places the reviewed studies in engineering, computing and the natural sciences, where work is judged above all on reproducibility and fair comparison with baselines.
future_directions.next_step: Report variance over repeated runs, compare against strong baselines on several datasets, run ablations and release the code
future_directions.feasibility_reason: needs compute time rather than new data

future_directions.title: Replication of single-study findings
future_directions.question: Which single-study findings survive an independent replication?
future_directions.rationale: The findings of Lindsay (2025), Wang et al. (2024), Khan (2025) and Žilinčík et al. (2023) have not been reported by any other reviewed study.
future_directions.next_step: Repeat each study's design and measures on a new sample, reporting the result whatever its direction
future_directions.feasibility_reason: the original protocols define what to do

future_directions.title: Scaling up the evidence on Cyber Warfare
future_directions.question: Does what is known about Cyber Warfare hold at larger scale and in other settings?
future_directions.rationale: The evidence so far comes from Estonia, Georgia, Ukraine, Iran, Russia, China and United States.
future_directions.next_step: Test Cyber Warfare in a larger, more varied sample; detecting a small effect (d = 0.2) at 80% power takes about 394 participants per group
future_directions.feasibility_reason: large samples need several recruitment sites

future_directions.title: Collaboration with the social sciences and human-computer interaction
future_directions.question: What would the social sciences and human-computer interaction add to research on Cyber Warfare?
future_directions.rationale: The reviewed studies work within engineering, computing and the natural sciences; the social sciences and human-computer interaction would add a perspective they do not cover.
future_directions.next_step: Combine the field's own methods with user studies and stakeholder interviews on how the systems are adopted, trusted and governed
future_directions.feasibility_reason: depends on finding collaborators and a shared research question
